items.title: Skeleton loading screens — rider pages
items.description: Add skeleton loading screens on the home page, ride search/listing page, and bookings page to eliminate the blank flash while data loads.
items.prompt_hint: While loading=true, show animate-pulse skeleton divs using bg-border that mirror the exact layout of the loaded content. Use rounded-xl for card skeletons, rounded-full for avatar/icon placeholders. When loading=false and data arrives, render the real content. Do not add a new component — inline the skeleton JSX in the existing conditional render.

items.title: Booking confirmation full-screen redesign
items.description: Redesign the booking confirmation page into a full-screen success state with the OTP prominently displayed so the rider can show it to the driver.
items.prompt_hint: Show: (1) large green checkmark icon (CheckCircle w-16 h-16 text-leaf), (2) 'Booking Confirmed!' in font-display text-2xl text-forest, (3) an OTP box: bg-forest rounded-2xl p-5, label 'Show this to your driver' in text-lime/60 text-xs uppercase, the OTP digits in font-mono text-4xl text-lime tracking-[0.3em]. Below the OTP box: route (from → to) in text-text font-semibold, departure date in text-sub. Add a 'View My Bookings' button linking to /bookings.

items.title: Seat availability visual pills on ride cards
items.description: Replace the plain text '4 seats available' on ride listing cards with a visual row of filled/empty circles showing booked vs available seats.
items.prompt_hint: For each ride card, render a row of circles (max 8 shown). Booked seats = filled circle (w-2.5 h-2.5 rounded-full bg-sub inline-block). Available seats = empty circle (w-2.5 h-2.5 rounded-full border border-leaf inline-block). Space them with gap-1. Cap at 8 circles even for larger vehicles. Keep existing seat count text as a subtitle in text-xs text-sub beneath the circles.

items.title: Empty states with CTA on rider pages
items.description: When data arrays are empty (not loading), show illustrated empty states with a call-to-action instead of blank sections.
items.prompt_hint: For bookings page empty state: Ticket icon (w-12 h-12 text-sub/40), heading 'No bookings yet' (text-lg font-semibold text-text), subtitle 'Your upcoming and past rides will appear here' (text-sm text-sub), CTA button 'Find a ride →' (bg-leaf text-white font-semibold px-5 py-3 rounded-xl) linking to /rides. For rides page with no results: Search icon, heading 'No rides found', subtitle 'Try different dates or cities', CTA 'Clear filters'. Wrap in a flex-col items-center py-16 gap-3 div.

items.title: Fare breakdown before booking confirmation
items.description: Show a per-seat × seat-count = total calculation before the user confirms booking, so there are no fare surprises.
items.prompt_hint: In the booking summary/confirmation step, add a fare breakdown row: '₹{farePerSeat} × {seats} seat{s} = ₹{total}' in text-sm text-sub. The total should be in font-display text-lg text-forest font-bold. Update dynamically when seat count changes. Convert from paise: fare_paise / 100. Place directly above the 'Book Now' / 'Confirm' button.

items.title: Route pages — Book CTA and fare estimate chip
items.description: Add a sticky 'Book this route' button and a live fare estimate chip to the /routes/[slug] SEO pages.
items.prompt_hint: Add a sticky bottom bar (fixed bottom-0 left-0 right-0 bg-white border-t border-border px-4 py-3 flex items-center justify-between z-10). Left side: 'From ₹{minFare}' in font-display text-xl text-forest (show only if fare data is available; omit if unknown). Right side: a Link to /rides?from={fromCity}&to={toCity} styled as bg-leaf text-white font-bold px-6 py-3 rounded-xl 'Book Now →'. Add pb-20 to the page content div to avoid content being hidden behind the sticky bar.

items.title: Offline detection banner
items.description: Show a banner when the user loses internet connection, with an auto-retry when they reconnect.
items.prompt_hint: Add a new 'use client' component OfflineBanner inside layout.tsx (not a separate file). Use useEffect to add/remove listeners on window 'online' and 'offline' events. When offline: render a fixed top banner (fixed top-0 inset-x-0 z-50 bg-gold text-white text-sm font-semibold text-center py-2 px-4 flex items-center justify-center gap-2). Show WifiOff icon from lucide-react and text 'You're offline — check your connection'. When back online: call toast.success('Back online') and hide the banner. The banner should animate in with transition-all.

items.title: Driver earnings 7-day bar chart
items.description: Add a 7-day earnings bar chart to the Earnings tab of the driver dashboard using only CSS — no charting library.
items.prompt_hint: In the earnings tab, above the existing earnings cards, add a 7-day chart. Compute last 7 calendar days from today (Asia/Kolkata). For each day, sum earnings from completed rides and requests that day. Render as a row of 7 bars: each bar is a flex-col items-center gap-1 div. The bar itself is a div with bg-leaf/80 rounded-t-lg w-8, height proportional to that day's earnings relative to the max (use inline style height: `${(dayEarnings/maxEarnings)*80}px`, min-height: 4px). Below: day label in text-[10px] text-sub (Mon/Tue/etc). Highlight today's bar with bg-leaf. Show '₹0' days as minimum height bars in bg-pale.

items.title: Dispatch card — show rider star rating
items.description: Show the rider's average star rating on the dispatch card before the driver accepts or rejects.
items.prompt_hint: In the PENDING dispatch card section, after the route/fare/date line, add a rider info row. Fetch the rider's rating from the existing request data (add avg_rating to the RideRequest select query if not already present, or use a placeholder 4.8 if unavailable). Render: Star icon (w-3 h-3 text-gold fill-gold) + '{rating} rider rating' in text-xs text-sub. Place this between the fare/date row and the notes (if any), before the Accept/Reject buttons.

items.title: Post Ride quick-action on driver home tab
items.description: Add a prominent 'Post a Ride' quick-action card on the driver dashboard Home tab so drivers can quickly post new rides.
items.prompt_hint: In the HOME tab section, when there is no active_dispatch, add a 'Post a Ride' quick-action card below the online toggle. Style: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4 flex items-center gap-4. Left: a rounded icon box bg-leaf/10 w-12 h-12 flex items-center justify-center with Plus icon text-leaf. Center: title 'Post a Ride' font-semibold text-text, subtitle 'Share your route and earn more' text-xs text-sub. Right: ArrowRight icon text-sub. Wrap the whole card in an <a href='/drivers/post-ride'> tag.

items.title: Rides tab — passenger count badge
items.description: Show a passenger count badge on each ride card in the driver dashboard Rides tab.
items.prompt_hint: On each ride card in the RIDES tab, add a passenger count indicator. Calculate booked seats: total_seats - available_seats. Show as a small badge next to the status badge: Users icon (w-3 h-3) + '{bookedSeats}/{totalSeats} passengers' in text-[10px] text-sub bg-pale px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded-full. Place it in the top-right area of the card next to the existing status badge, or on a second line below the route.

items.title: Schedule tab — available days summary chip
items.description: Show a summary chip at the top of the Schedule tab telling the driver how many days this month they're available.
items.prompt_hint: At the top of the SCHEDULE tab (before the AvailabilityCalendar), add a summary chip. Count the days in the current month that are NOT marked as rest days in localAvail. Show: bg-pale rounded-full px-4 py-2 inline-flex items-center gap-2, CalendarDays icon text-leaf w-4 h-4, text '{n} available days this month' in text-sm font-semibold text-text. If n === 0, change the bg to bg-gold/10 and text to text-gold to prompt the driver to mark availability.

items.title: Me tab — profile completion progress bar
items.description: Add a profile completion progress bar on the Me tab showing the driver what they still need to fill in.
items.prompt_hint: In the PROFILE tab, above the form inputs, add a completion meter. Check which fields have values: name (profileForm.name), license_number, vehicle_number, vehicle_model. Score = filled fields / 4. Render: a label 'Profile {score*100}% complete' in text-sm font-semibold text-text, then a progress bar: bg-pale rounded-full h-2 w-full with an inner div bg-leaf rounded-full h-2 style={{width: `${score*100}%`}} transition-all. Below the bar, if score < 1: list missing fields in text-xs text-sub as 'Missing: name, licence number' etc.

items.title: Loading skeletons on all driver dashboard tabs
items.description: Add per-tab loading skeletons to the driver dashboard so tabs show a skeleton instead of an empty state while data loads.
items.prompt_hint: The dashboard already has loadingRequests and loadingRides state. Add similar loadingEarnings state initialized to false, set to true when earnings tab loads, false when done. For each tab that has a loading state, when loading is true show 3 skeleton cards: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4 animate-pulse with inner divs of bg-border rounded-lg h-4 w-3/4 mb-2 and bg-border rounded-lg h-3 w-1/2. This replaces the immediate empty state that currently shows while data loads.

items.title: Fleet utilization card on owner dashboard
items.description: Add a fleet utilization percentage card to the owner dashboard showing how many vehicles are active vs total.
items.prompt_hint: Fetch the vehicles count from the existing dashboard data (or from /api/fleet/vehicles if not already loaded). Show a new card: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-5. Title: 'Fleet Utilization' in text-xs font-bold text-sub uppercase. Large number: '{activeCount}/{totalCount}' in font-display text-3xl text-forest. Subtitle: '{pct}% active' in text-sm text-sub. A simple progress bar: bg-pale h-2 rounded-full with inner bg-leaf rounded-full width={pct}%. Place this card in the existing stats grid on the dashboard.

items.title: My Fleet top summary bar
items.description: Add a summary bar at the top of the My Fleet page showing active / inactive / unassigned vehicle counts at a glance.
items.prompt_hint: After the page header row, add a 3-column summary bar: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4 grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 mb-4. Each column: number in font-display text-2xl (text-leaf for active, text-sub for inactive, text-gold for unassigned), label in text-[10px] text-sub uppercase. Active = vehicles.filter(v => v.active).length. Inactive = vehicles.filter(v => !v.active).length. Unassigned = vehicles.filter(v => !v.driver_id).length. Only render this bar when !loading and vehicles.length > 0.

items.title: Earnings per vehicle breakdown table
items.description: Add a per-vehicle earnings breakdown table to the owner earnings page.
items.prompt_hint: Group the existing bookings data by ride_id vehicle. The bookings from /api/fleet/earnings already contain Ride data. Group by ride vehicle (you'll need to cross-reference with vehicle data if available, or group by driver). Show a table below the existing payouts section: 'Earnings by Trip' heading, then each booking as a row with columns: route (from_city → to_city), date (departure_time formatted), amount (₹{amount_paise/100}), status badge. Wrap in bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl overflow-hidden. Use a simple div table pattern (not an HTML table) with flex rows.

items.title: Fleet Drivers — trips this week column
items.description: Add a 'trips this week' count to each driver card on the Fleet Drivers page.
items.prompt_hint: The driver data from /api/fleet/fleet-drivers includes Vehicle data. Add a 'Trips this week' count to each driver card. Fetch from /api/fleet/history with the driver_profile_id as a filter query param (GET /api/fleet/history?driver_profile_id={id}&days=7). Show the count as a small chip: Route icon w-3 h-3 + '{count} trips this week' in text-xs text-sub. If the fetch fails or returns 0, show '0 trips this week'. Fetch per-driver in a useEffect after drivers load.

items.title: Owner dashboard — alert dot for unassigned drivers
items.description: Show an alert indicator on the owner dashboard when there are approved fleet drivers who have no assigned vehicle.
items.prompt_hint: After loading dashboard data, also fetch /api/fleet/fleet-drivers. Count drivers where vehicles array is empty (no assigned vehicle). If count > 0, show an alert banner in the dashboard: bg-gold/10 border border-gold/30 rounded-2xl p-4 flex items-center gap-3. AlertCircle icon text-gold w-5 h-5. Text: '{count} driver{s} {have/has} no assigned vehicle.' in text-sm text-text. Link: 'Assign now →' text-leaf font-semibold href='/fleet/fleet-drivers'. Place this banner below the stats grid.

items.title: Vehicle card — inline Assign Driver dropdown
items.description: Add an inline Assign Driver dropdown directly on vehicle cards on the My Fleet page, eliminating the need to navigate to the Fleet Drivers page to assign.
items.prompt_hint: On each vehicle card where driver_id is null, add an 'Assign Driver' section below the existing card content. Fetch approved drivers from /api/fleet/fleet-drivers on page load alongside vehicles. Show a select dropdown: border border-border rounded-xl px-3 py-2 text-xs w-full. Options: 'Assign a driver…' (disabled default) + each driver's name + phone. On change, call POST /api/fleet/assign-driver with {vehicle_id, driver_profile_id}. On success: toast.success + update local vehicles state to set driver_id. On error: toast.error.

items.title: Owner dashboard — monthly revenue trend chart
items.description: Add a mini monthly revenue trend chart to the owner dashboard showing earnings over the last 6 months.
items.prompt_hint: Fetch /api/fleet/earnings. Group bookings by month (last 6 months). For each month compute total amount_paise. Render a CSS-only bar chart: flex items-end gap-2 h-20. Each bar: flex-1 bg-leaf/70 rounded-t-lg with height proportional to that month's revenue relative to the max (inline style). Below each bar: 3-letter month label in text-[10px] text-sub text-center. Add a 'Last 6 months' label and total in font-display text-2xl text-forest above the chart. Wrap in a bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-5 card.

items.title: Admin metrics bar
items.description: Add a key metrics bar to the top of the admin dashboard showing today's bookings, active rides, and new signups.
items.prompt_hint: Fetch /api/admin/requests (already done on this page). Additionally fetch /api/admin/applicants for new signups. Add a 3-column metrics bar at the top of the Dashboard component: bg-forest rounded-2xl p-5 grid grid-cols-3 gap-4 text-white mb-6. Column 1: today's confirmed+completed bookings count, label 'Today's Bookings' text-lime/60. Column 2: confirmed rides currently (status CONFIRMED), label 'Active Rides'. Column 3: applicants submitted today (created_at >= today), label 'New Signups'. Each metric: font-display text-3xl text-lime + text-xs label.

items.title: Admin applicants — bulk approve/reject
items.description: Add bulk select checkboxes and a bulk approve/reject action bar to the admin applicants page.
items.prompt_hint: Add a selectedIds: Set<string> state. Add a checkbox to each applicant card (top-left corner, w-4 h-4 accent-green-700). Add a sticky bottom action bar that appears when selectedIds.size > 0: fixed bottom-0 inset-x-0 bg-white border-t border-border px-4 py-3 flex items-center justify-between z-20. Left: '{n} selected'. Right: 'Approve All' button (bg-leaf text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-xl text-sm font-bold) and 'Reject All' button (border border-red-300 text-red-500 px-4 py-2 rounded-xl text-sm font-bold). Bulk action calls the existing single-item approve/reject API endpoint in a Promise.all loop.

items.title: Admin drivers list — search and status filter
items.description: Add a search input and status filter tabs to the admin drivers page.
items.prompt_hint: Add: (1) a search input above the driver list: border border-border rounded-xl px-4 py-2.5 text-sm w-full placeholder 'Search by name or phone…'. Filter the in-memory drivers array by name.toLowerCase().includes(query) || phone.includes(query). (2) Status filter tabs below the search: 'All' | 'Pending' | 'Approved' | 'Rejected' as button tabs (active: bg-leaf text-white, inactive: bg-pale text-sub) text-sm font-semibold px-4 py-2 rounded-xl. Show filtered count in each tab label: 'Approved (12)'. Both filters compose: show drivers matching BOTH search and status filter.

items.title: Admin documents — pending count badge and verification ring
items.description: Add a pending documents count badge to the page header and a per-driver verification progress ring.
items.prompt_hint: Add: (1) A count badge next to the 'Documents' page title: bg-red-500 text-white text-xs font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full showing the number of documents with status PENDING. (2) For each driver group in the document list, show a verification progress ring next to their name: a small SVG circle (32×32, stroke-dasharray technique) showing verified_count/total_docs_count. Filled arc in stroke-leaf, empty arc in stroke-border. Below the ring: '{n}/{total}' in text-[10px] text-sub. This gives at-a-glance sense of how many docs are cleared per driver.

items.title: Admin dispatch — manual dispatch button
items.description: Add a manual dispatch button on the admin dispatch page that lets the admin force-dispatch a specific ride request to a specific driver.
items.prompt_hint: Add a 'Manual Dispatch' button at the top of the page (bg-leaf text-white font-bold px-4 py-2.5 rounded-xl). On click, show an inline form: a select for pending ride requests (fetched from /api/admin/requests?status=PENDING), a select for approved drivers (fetched from /api/admin/drivers), and a 'Dispatch' button. On submit: POST /api/admin/dispatch with {request_id, driver_id}. On success: toast.success('Dispatched successfully') and refresh the dispatch list. On error: toast.error(json.error). Use a simple show/hide toggle for the form — no modal.

items.title: Admin used cars — status filter and inquiry badge
items.description: Add status filter tabs and an inquiry count badge to listing cards on the admin used cars page.
items.prompt_hint: Add: (1) Status filter tabs: 'All' | 'Active' | 'Sold' | 'Inactive' — same tab styling as other admin filter tabs (bg-leaf active, bg-pale inactive). Filter the in-memory listings array. Show count in each tab label. (2) On each listing card, add an inquiry count badge: bg-leaf/10 text-leaf text-xs font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full '{n} inquiries' — fetch inquiry counts from /api/admin/used-cars/{id}/inquiries or use a pre-fetched count if already in the listing data. If the listing data doesn't include inquiry_count, add it to the GET fetch by including a count query.

items.title: Cross-portal 'What's new' chip in portal headers
items.description: Add a subtle 'What's new' chip to the header of each portal showing the most recent improvement that went live.
items.prompt_hint: Fetch GET /api/admin/improvements (no auth needed for a public summary endpoint — add a public variant). Return the most recent completed improvement: {day, title, completed_at}. In each portal header, show a small chip: bg-leaf/10 text-leaf text-[10px] font-semibold px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full '✨ Day {n}: {title}'. On click/tap expand to show the full title. Cache in sessionStorage so it only fetches once per session. Place in the header row, right-aligned, after other header elements.

items.title: Mobile polish pass — modals and scroll
items.description: Fix mobile UX issues: ensure all modals/sheets close on browser back button, fix overscroll on iOS, ensure tap targets are all ≥44px.
items.prompt_hint: For any bottom sheets or modals that open inline (not using Radix/Vaul): add a useEffect that pushes a history entry on open (history.pushState(null, '', window.location.href)) and listens to popstate to close. Add overscroll-y-none to any full-height scroll containers. Audit all interactive buttons in these files: any with only icon children need explicit w-11 h-11 min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px] classes. Add touch-manipulation to all button elements to remove 300ms tap delay.

items.title: Performance pass — lazy load and layout shift
items.description: Reduce cumulative layout shift and improve load time by lazy-loading images and adding preconnect hints.
items.prompt_hint: In layout.tsx : add and . For any tags (not Next.js Image): add loading='lazy' decoding='async'. For vehicle thumbnail images in fleet/vehicles/page.tsx: wrap in a div with a fixed aspect-square and bg-pale placeholder so the layout doesn't shift when the image loads. For ride listing cards in rides/page.tsx: add min-h-[120px] to each card so the skeleton and loaded card have the same height.

items.title: Rider bookings — visual trip status timeline
items.description: Add a horizontal step-progress timeline to each booking card showing which stage the trip is at: Pending → Confirmed → In Progress → Done.
items.prompt_hint: Inside each booking card (after the from/to row), add a horizontal 4-step timeline. Steps: ['Pending', 'Confirmed', 'In Progress', 'Done']. Compute activeStep from booking.status: PENDING=0, CONFIRMED=1, IN_PROGRESS=2, COMPLETED=3, CANCELLED=-1. Render: <div className='flex items-center gap-0 mt-3 mb-1'>. For each step: a circle (w-5 h-5 rounded-full text-[9px] flex items-center justify-center font-bold) that is bg-leaf text-white if step <= activeStep, else bg-pale text-sub. Between circles: a <div className='flex-1 h-0.5'> that is bg-leaf if the connecting segment is passed, else bg-pale. Below each circle (absolute or flex col): a label in text-[8px] text-sub text-center. Skip the timeline entirely if status is CANCELLED — show a red 'Cancelled' chip instead. Do NOT show timeline for CANCELLED trips.

items.title: Rider profile — trip count and member badge
items.description: Enrich the rider profile page with a trip count stat, member-since date, and a loyalty tier badge.
items.prompt_hint: Fetch GET /api/requests?mine=true (or whichever endpoint returns the rider's own bookings — check the file's existing fetch calls). Count completed trips. Below the user's name and phone number add a 3-column stats row: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4 grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 mb-4. Column 1: completed trip count with label 'Trips'. Column 2: member since date (format: user.created_at formatted as 'MMM YYYY' using toLocaleDateString('en-IN', {month:'short', year:'numeric', timeZone:'Asia/Kolkata'})) with label 'Member since'. Column 3: a tier badge based on trip count: 0–4 = 'Explorer' bg-pale text-sub, 5–19 = 'Regular' bg-leaf/10 text-leaf, 20+ = 'Elite' bg-gold/10 text-gold. Each stat: font-display text-xl text-forest value + text-[10px] text-sub uppercase tracking-wide label.

items.title: Trip tracker — live auto-refresh polling
items.description: Make the public trip tracker page auto-refresh every 30 seconds so riders see status updates without manually reloading.
items.prompt_hint:
Find the existing data-fetching useEffect (the one that fetches trip info by id). Extract the fetch logic into a named async function (e.g., fetchTrip). Call it once on mount. Then set up a polling interval: const interval = setInterval(fetchTrip, 30000). Clear it in the cleanup function and also clear it when trip.status === 'COMPLETED' (no need to poll a done trip). Add a 'Last updated' timestamp: a state lastUpdated = new Date(). Update it after each successful fetch. Show it below the status badge:

Updated {lastUpdated.toLocaleTimeString('en-IN', {timeZone:'Asia/Kolkata'})}

. Also add a 'Refresh now' text link next to the timestamp that calls fetchTrip manually.

items.title: Receipt page — print-friendly layout and copy-link button
items.description: Add a print button and a copy-link button to the trip receipt page, and add print-friendly CSS so the page renders cleanly when printed.
items.prompt_hint: Add two action buttons below the existing WhatsApp share button. Button 1: 'Copy Link' — calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(window.location.href) then shows toast.success('Link copied!'). Use a Copy icon from lucide-react (import Link2). Button 2: 'Print' — calls window.print(). Use a Printer icon (already imported). Both buttons: flex items-center gap-2 border border-border rounded-xl px-4 py-2.5 text-sm font-semibold text-sub w-full justify-center. Stack all 3 share buttons vertically with gap-2. Add a <style> block (JSX dangerouslySetInnerHTML or a <style jsx> tag) with @media print rules: hide the action buttons, remove padding, set background white, remove rounded corners from cards. Use className='print:hidden' on the button container.

items.title: Rider bookings — rate completed trip prompt
items.description: Show a star-rating prompt card for the most recent completed trip that hasn't been rated yet, using localStorage to track dismissal.
items.prompt_hint: Add a 'Rate your trip' inline card for the most-recent COMPLETED booking. State: const [rated, setRated] = useState<string | null>(null); const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(0); const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false). On mount: check localStorage.getItem('gr_rated_' + booking.id). If already rated or dismissed, skip. Render a card at the very top of the bookings list (before the list) when there is a qualifying booking: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4 mb-4. Content: 'How was your trip to {to_city}?' in font-semibold text-text text-sm. 5 stars in a row: ★ characters, text-2xl, text-gold if index <= hovered or <= submitted_rating else text-pale. On star click: call POST /api/bookings/{id}/rate with {rating: n}, then localStorage.setItem('gr_rated_' + id, String(n)), setSubmitted(true). On 'Maybe later' link click: localStorage.setItem('gr_rated_' + id, 'dismissed'), hide card.

items.title: Booking search — recent routes quick-fill chips
items.description: Show up to 3 recent route chips below the search form that pre-fill the from/to fields when tapped.
items.prompt_hint: Add a recentRoutes: {from: string; to: string}[] state. On mount: parse localStorage.getItem('gr_recent_routes') (JSON array, max 3 items). After a successful search (when the user submits the search form and results load), save the search pair: const routes = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('gr_recent_routes') || '[]'); const updated = [{from, to}, ...routes.filter(r => !(r.from===from && r.to===to))].slice(0,3); localStorage.setItem('gr_recent_routes', JSON.stringify(updated)). Render the chips between the search form and the results list (only when recentRoutes.length > 0 AND no results showing yet): <div className='flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-1 mt-2'>. Each chip: <button onClick={() => {setFrom(r.from); setTo(r.to);}} className='flex-shrink-0 flex items-center gap-1 bg-white border border-border rounded-full px-3 py-1.5 text-xs text-sub font-medium'>{r.from} → {r.to}</button>. Look at the existing state variables for from/to (they may be named differently in the file) and adapt accordingly.

items.title: Used car detail — image gallery navigation
items.description: Add prev/next navigation arrows to the used car detail page photo gallery so users can browse all photos.
items.prompt_hint:
Find where the car's photos are displayed (likely an images array or photos array from the fetched listing data). Add a photoIndex: number state (default 0). Wrap the main photo in a relative container:
. Show the current photo as . Add a left arrow button: . Right arrow: same with Math.min(photos.length-1, i+1) and ›. Hide left arrow when photoIndex===0, hide right arrow when photoIndex===photos.length-1 (use conditional rendering). Below: dot indicators:
. Each dot:
. If the file uses a single image (no array), skip the navigation and just add proper rounded-2xl aspect-video styling.

items.title: Driver dashboard — today's earnings summary
items.description: Add a 'Today's earnings' mini card to the driver dashboard home tab showing today's total and trip count.
items.prompt_hint: Find where the driver's ride data is fetched (completed rides). Filter rides whose travel_date === today (compare ISO date strings with new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]). Compute todayTrips (count) and todayEarnings (sum of fare_paise / 100). Add a card just above the status toggle section (or at the top of the home tab content): <div className='grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 mb-4'>. Left cell: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4. Top: text-[10px] text-sub uppercase tracking-wide 'Today'. Value: font-display text-2xl text-forest '₹{todayEarnings}'. Right cell: same styling. Top: 'Trips today'. Value: font-display text-2xl text-forest '{todayTrips}'. If no rides data is available on the home tab (rides fetched only on the rides tab), compute from whatever earnings/stats data is already fetched on the home tab. If nothing is available, show '—' as the value.

items.title: Driver dashboard — star rating display on Me tab
items.description: Replace the raw numeric rating on the driver Me tab with rendered star icons and a context label.
items.prompt_hint:
Find where the driver's avg_rating is displayed (on the Me/Profile tab). Replace the raw number display with a star row. Create a StarRating component inline: function StarRating({ rating }: { rating: number }) { return (
{[1,2,3,4,5].map(i => (★))}{rating.toFixed(1)}
); }. Show it below the driver's name. Also add a context label below the stars: text-[10px] text-sub 'Based on passenger ratings'. If avg_rating is 0 or null, show 'No ratings yet' in text-sub text-sm instead of the stars.

items.title: Driver post-ride form — field completion progress bar
items.description: Add a progress bar at the top of the post-ride form showing how many required fields have been filled.
items.prompt_hint:
Identify all required form fields in the post-ride form (look for the form state variables). Create a derived value: const filledCount = [field1, field2, ...].filter(v => v !== '' && v !== null && v !== undefined).length; const totalRequired = . Compute percent = Math.round((filledCount / totalRequired) * 100). At the top of the form (below the page title, above the first input): render a progress section:
Form completion{filledCount}/{totalRequired} fields
. The bar color transitions from leaf (green) at all fill levels. Only count fields that are truly required (not optional notes fields).

items.title: Driver KYC — document upload status badges
items.description: Add color-coded status badges to each document slot on the driver KYC page showing pending/approved/rejected state.
items.prompt_hint: For each document type displayed on the KYC page, show a status badge next to the document name. The document objects fetched from the API should have a status field (e.g., 'PENDING', 'APPROVED', 'REJECTED', or null if not uploaded). Badge styling: APPROVED → bg-leaf/10 text-leaf text-[10px] font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full 'Approved'. PENDING → bg-gold/10 text-gold text-[10px] font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full 'Under review'. REJECTED → bg-red-50 text-red-500 text-[10px] font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full 'Rejected'. null (not uploaded) → bg-pale text-sub text-[10px] font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full 'Not uploaded'. Also add a KYC overall progress bar at the top of the page: count approved docs / total doc types. Same h-1.5 bg-pale rounded-full bar with bg-leaf fill. Label: '{n} of {total} documents verified'.

items.title: Fleet drivers — star rating display and online sort
items.description: Display avg_rating as star icons on each driver card and sort drivers by online status (online first).
items.prompt_hint: 1) Sort the drivers array before rendering: const sorted = [...drivers].sort((a,b) => (b.is_online ? 1 : 0) - (a.is_online ? 1 : 0)). Use sorted in the map. 2) In each driver card, replace or augment the existing trips badge area with a star rating display. After the 'trips' badge, add: {[1,2,3,4,5].map(i => ({i <= Math.round(d.avg_rating ?? 0) ? '★' : '☆'}))}{d.avg_rating ? d.avg_rating.toFixed(1) : '—'}. Wrap the trip badge and star rating in a flex items-center gap-2 container. If avg_rating is null or 0, show '☆☆☆☆☆ —' so the layout is consistent.

items.title: Fleet history — earnings summary header
items.description: Add a summary header above the trip history list showing total trips completed and total earnings for the loaded period.
items.prompt_hint:
Read the file to find where trips/bookings are stored in state (the history list). After the list loads, compute: totalTrips = trips.length; totalEarnings = trips.reduce((sum, t) => sum + (t.fare_paise ?? 0), 0) / 100. Add a summary card below the page header and above the trip list:
. Left:

Total Trips

{totalTrips}

. Right:

Total Earned

₹{totalEarnings.toLocaleString('en-IN')}

. Only show this card when trips.length > 0. If fare field is named differently (check the trip interface), adapt accordingly.

items.title: Fleet today — active dispatch ETA card
items.description: Add a prominent ETA/status card at the top of the fleet today page when a dispatch is active, showing the current trip stage.
items.prompt_hint:
Read the file to find the active dispatch/trip state variable. When there is an active (CONFIRMED or IN_PROGRESS) dispatch, render a prominent status card at the very top of the page content:
. Content:

{status === 'CONFIRMED' ? 'Driver on the way' : 'Trip in progress'}

.

{trip.from_city} → {trip.to_city}

.
{trip.travel_date formatted as 'dd MMM'}{trip.total_seats} seats
. If eta_min is available on the trip object:

ETA: ~{eta_min} min

. If not available, omit the ETA line.

items.title: Fleet notifications — mark all read button
items.description: Add a 'Mark all as read' button to the fleet notifications page and visually distinguish unread from read notifications.
items.prompt_hint: Read the file to find the notifications state and how read/unread is tracked. Add a 'Mark all read' button in the page header row (right side): <button onClick={markAllRead} className='text-xs text-leaf font-semibold'>Mark all read</button>. The markAllRead function should call PATCH /api/fleet/notifications/read-all (with Bearer token) and then update local state to set all notifications' read field to true. Also update visual styling: unread notifications should have a left border accent: border-l-2 border-leaf bg-leaf/5 (add this to the card className when !n.read). Read notifications: normal bg-white border border-border. If the API endpoint path is different (check existing fetch calls in the file), adapt the URL accordingly. If there's no is_read or read field, look for a different field name in the notification interface.

items.title: Fleet availability — quick today toggle
items.description: Add a 'Quick toggle' hero section at the top of the availability page to set today's availability with one tap.
items.prompt_hint:
Read the file to understand how availability is managed (likely a list of dates or a toggle per date). Add a 'Today' section at the top of the page (above any existing availability list):
. Left side:

Today

{new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-IN', {weekday:'long', day:'numeric', month:'long', timeZone:'Asia/Kolkata'})}

. Right side: a toggle button. If today is marked available: . If not: . The toggleToday function should call the same API endpoint used for setting availability for a date, with today's ISO date string. Derive todayAvailable from the existing availability state.

items.title: Fleet profile — fleet stats and member since
items.description: Enrich the fleet driver/owner profile page with a stats row showing fleet size, total trips, and member-since date.
items.prompt_hint: Read the file to find the profile data structure (user info, driver profile). Below the user's name and phone number, add a stats row: <div className='grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 mb-4'>. Each cell: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-3 text-center. Cell 1: value = total_trips (from driver profile or fetched separately), label 'Trips'. Cell 2: value = member since date formatted as 'MMM YYYY' (from user.created_at or profile.created_at), label 'Member since'. Cell 3: value = avg_rating displayed as '{rating.toFixed(1)} ★', label 'Avg rating' (use text-gold for the ★). Each cell: font-display text-xl text-forest for the value, text-[10px] text-sub uppercase tracking-wide for the label. If any value is unavailable (null or undefined), show '—'. If total_trips is not in the fetched data, count from the history endpoint if already fetched, otherwise show '—'.

items.title: Fleet earnings — period filter tabs
items.description: Add period filter tabs (This Month / Last Month / All Time) to the fleet earnings page to filter the payouts list.
items.prompt_hint: Add a period: 'this_month' | 'last_month' | 'all' state (default: 'all'). Below the bar chart and above the payouts list, render 3 filter tabs: <div className='flex gap-2 mb-4 overflow-x-auto pb-1'>. Tab: <button className={period===key ? 'bg-leaf text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-full text-xs font-bold flex-shrink-0' : 'bg-white border border-border text-sub px-4 py-2 rounded-full text-xs font-semibold flex-shrink-0'}>. Labels: 'This Month', 'Last Month', 'All Time'. Filter the payouts in render: const now = new Date(); const thisMonthStart = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 1); const lastMonthStart = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth()-1, 1); const lastMonthEnd = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 0); const filtered = period==='all' ? payouts : period==='this_month' ? payouts.filter(p => new Date(p.period_to) >= thisMonthStart) : payouts.filter(p => new Date(p.period_to) >= lastMonthStart && new Date(p.period_to) <= lastMonthEnd). Use filtered for the list render. Show a filtered total above the list: 'Total: ₹{filteredSum.toLocaleString('en-IN')}' in font-display text-xl text-forest.

items.title: Admin bookings — search and status filter
items.description: Add a search input and status filter tabs to the admin bookings page so admins can quickly find rides.
items.prompt_hint: Add a search: string state (default ''). Above the existing filter tabs (or above the list if no tabs exist), add a search input: <input value={search} onChange={e => setSearch(e.target.value)} placeholder='Search by phone or city…' className='w-full border border-border rounded-xl px-4 py-2.5 text-sm mb-3 outline-none focus:ring-2 ring-leaf/30 bg-white' />. Filter the in-memory requests array by both search and current status filter: const visible = requests.filter(r => { const matchesSearch = !search || r.rider_phone.includes(search) || r.from_city.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase()) || r.to_city.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase()); const matchesStatus = !statusFilter || r.status === statusFilter; return matchesSearch && matchesStatus; }). If status filter tabs don't exist yet, add them: 'All' | 'PENDING' | 'CONFIRMED' | 'COMPLETED' | 'CANCELLED'. Tab style: active = bg-leaf text-white, inactive = bg-pale text-sub. Each tab shows a count badge in parentheses based on the unfiltered array. Show a count label above the list: '{visible.length} bookings'.

items.title: Admin payouts — summary stats bar
items.description: Add a summary stats bar to the admin payouts page showing total pending payout amount and total paid to date.
items.prompt_hint:
Read the file to find the payouts state. Compute: pendingTotal = payouts.filter(p => p.status === 'PENDING').reduce((s, p) => s + p.amount_paise, 0) / 100; paidTotal = payouts.filter(p => p.status === 'PAID').reduce((s, p) => s + p.amount_paise, 0) / 100; pendingCount = payouts.filter(p => p.status === 'PENDING').length. Add a stats card above the payouts list:
. Left cell: bg-gold/10 border border-gold/20 rounded-2xl p-4.

Pending Payouts

₹{pendingTotal.toLocaleString('en-IN')}

{pendingCount} payouts

. Right cell: bg-leaf/10 border border-leaf/20 rounded-2xl p-4.

Paid Out

₹{paidTotal.toLocaleString('en-IN')}

. Only show this bar when payouts.length > 0. If the status values are different (check the interface), adapt filter strings accordingly.

items.title: Admin fares — bulk percentage adjustment
items.description: Add a bulk percentage increase/decrease control to the admin fares page so all fares can be adjusted at once.
items.prompt_hint: Add states: bulkPct: string (default ''), bulkMode: boolean (default false), bulkSaving: boolean. Add a 'Bulk Adjust' button in the header row (right side): <button onClick={() => setBulkMode(b => !b)} className='bg-pale text-sub text-xs font-semibold px-3 py-2 rounded-xl'>Bulk Adjust</button>. When bulkMode is true, show an inline panel below the header: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4 mb-4. Content: 'Adjust all fares by:' label. A row with: a text input for percentage (type='number', min=-50, max=100, value=bulkPct, onChange updates bulkPct), '%' suffix label, then two buttons: 'Increase' (bg-leaf text-white) and 'Decrease' (bg-red-50 text-red-500 border border-red-200). The Increase button multiplies all in-memory fares by (1 + pct/100) and the Decrease button by (1 - pct/100). Apply to all fares: update the local fares state (round to nearest integer paise). Show a preview below: 'Preview: {n} fares adjusted'. Also add a 'Save all' button that calls the existing fare update endpoint for each fare in a loop. Use a saving spinner (Loader2) on Save.

items.title: Admin activity log — action-type filter tabs
items.description: Add action-type filter tabs to the admin activity log so admins can filter by booking, driver, or system events.
items.prompt_hint: Read the file to understand the log entry structure (action field, entity type, etc.). Add a logFilter: string state (default 'all'). Below the page header, add filter tabs: derive unique action categories from the logs array. Common categories to look for: 'booking', 'driver', 'payout', 'config', 'auth'. Tab: 'All' plus each unique category that exists in the loaded logs. Tab style: active = bg-leaf text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-full text-xs font-bold, inactive = bg-white border border-border text-sub px-4 py-2 rounded-full text-xs font-semibold. Overflow-x-auto container. Filter visible logs: logs.filter(l => logFilter === 'all' || l.action_type === logFilter || l.entity?.toLowerCase().includes(logFilter)). Adapt the filter logic to match whatever field names the log entry interface actually uses. Show count after filter: '{filtered.length} entries'.

items.title: Admin improvements — portal color badges and mini chart
items.description: Improve the improvements audit trail page with portal color badges, area labels, and a mini completion bar chart.
items.prompt_hint:
Read the file to find the ImprovementLog data structure. 1) Add a portal color badge to each log entry. PORTAL_COLORS: { rider: 'bg-blue-50 text-blue-600', driver: 'bg-gold/10 text-gold', fleet: 'bg-leaf/10 text-leaf', admin: 'bg-forest/10 text-forest', all: 'bg-pale text-sub' }. Show a badge: {log.portal}. 2) Add an AREA badge next to it: area==='ux' → 'bg-purple-50 text-purple-600', area==='feature' → 'bg-leaf/10 text-leaf', area==='perf' → 'bg-gold/10 text-gold'. 3) At the top of the page, add a completion bar: total improvements in the system vs completed. Compute from the logs.

{completed} of {total} improvements shipped

.

items.title: Admin vehicles — summary stats and assignment status
items.description: Add a summary stats bar to the admin vehicles page showing total vehicles, how many are assigned to drivers, and how many have pending photo approval.
items.prompt_hint: Read the file to find the vehicles state. Compute: total = vehicles.length; assigned = vehicles.filter(v => v.driver_id).length; pendingPhotos = vehicles.filter(v => v.photo_status === 'PENDING' || v.photo_url && !v.photo_approved).length (adapt to actual field names). Add a 3-column stats bar below the page header: <div className='grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 mb-4'>. Each cell: bg-white border border-border rounded-xl p-3 text-center. Cell 1: value=total, label='Total'. Cell 2: value=assigned, label='Assigned'. Cell 3: value=(total-assigned), label='Unassigned'. Each: font-display text-2xl text-forest value + text-[10px] text-sub uppercase tracking-wide label. Also add an assignment status badge to each vehicle card: if driver_id → bg-leaf/10 text-leaf 'Assigned', else → bg-pale text-sub 'Unassigned'. Badge: text-[10px] font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full. Place it in the top-right of the card.

items.title: Admin fleet owners — fleet size and approval status
items.description: Add fleet size (vehicle count), driver count, and approval status badges to each owner card on the admin owners page.
items.prompt_hint: Read the file to understand the owner data structure (the interface for fleet owner entries). Each owner should have or be augmented with: vehicle count and driver count (may be nested arrays or counts). Add to each owner card: 1) A 2-column mini stats row: '<vehicles> vehicles · <drivers> drivers' in text-xs text-sub. If these counts aren't in the data, show what is available (e.g., just vehicle_count if that field exists). 2) An approval status badge in the top-right of the card. Use the owner's status or approval field: APPROVED → bg-leaf/10 text-leaf 'Active', PENDING → bg-gold/10 text-gold 'Pending', REJECTED or INACTIVE → bg-pale text-sub 'Inactive'. Badge: text-[10px] font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full. 3) At the top of the page add a summary: total owners count and active owners count in a 2-column card: bg-white border border-border rounded-2xl p-4 mb-4 grid grid-cols-2 gap-4.

items.title: Admin commission — earnings impact preview
items.description: When editing a commission rate, show a live preview of how the change would affect total driver earnings based on recent revenue.
items.prompt_hint:
Read the file to find: the commission rate state variable(s), and whether there is recent revenue data available. Add a preview section that appears when the admin has edited a commission value. State: editingKey: string | null (which commission entry is being edited), previewRate: number | null. When editing a commission row, show an inline preview below the input:
At {previewRate}% commission: drivers keep ₹{Math.round(recentRevenue * (1 - previewRate/100)).toLocaleString('en-IN')} of every ₹{recentRevenue.toLocaleString('en-IN')} earned
. If recent revenue data is not available on this page, use a hardcoded example: 'For every ₹10,000 earned, drivers receive ₹{(10000 * (1 - previewRate/100)).toLocaleString('en-IN')}'. The preview updates live as the input changes (compute from the controlled input value). Only show it when previewRate is not null and is a valid number (0-100).

items.title: Admin config — unsaved changes indicator
items.description: Add an unsaved-changes banner and a discard button to the remote config page so admins don't accidentally lose edits.
items.prompt_hint:
Read the file to find how config values are stored and edited (likely a config object state and a separate editedConfig state or individual field states). Add a isDirty derived state: const isDirty = JSON.stringify(config) !== JSON.stringify(editedConfig) (or compare the relevant fields). When isDirty is true, show a sticky banner below the header:
. Left: ⚠ Unsaved changes. Right: two buttons: 'Discard' (text-xs text-sub font-semibold, onClick resets editedConfig to the original config) and 'Save' (bg-leaf text-white text-xs font-bold px-3 py-1.5 rounded-lg, calls the existing save function). If the page uses a single save button elsewhere, keep it but also add the sticky banner. If the page has no separate edited state (edits directly mutate config), introduce a localConfig state initialized from config, and save pushes localConfig.

items.title: Booking confirm — trip summary and fare breakdown
items.description: Improve the booking confirmation page with a clear fare breakdown card showing base fare, per-seat calculation, and a total.

Read the file to find the booking data (fare, seats, route). Add a fare breakdown card below the trip details:
. Title:

Fare Breakdown

. Rows: flex justify-between text-sm. Row 1: 'Base fare per seat' / '₹{perSeatFare}'. Row 2 (if seats > 1): 'Seats booked' / '{seats}'. A divider:
. Total row: 'Total' in font-bold / '₹{totalFare}' in font-display text-lg text-leaf. Compute: totalFare = fare_paise / 100 (or however it's stored), perSeatFare = totalFare / seats. Format with .toLocaleString('en-IN'). Below the breakdown, add a muted policy note:

Cancellation is free up to 2 hours before departure

. Keep all existing page content — only add the new card.

items.title: Used cars sell form — photo upload preview grid

items.prompt_hint:

Quick Actions
